Guidance & outlook: On behalf of PhillipCapital (India) Private Limited, we welcome you to the Q1 FY27 call of JK Lakshmi Cement Limited.
Also, the participants of the call can download a copy of the Q1 FY27 Results Presentation from the company website.
Total for FY27 in 12 months period we expect a total capex of about INR1,500 crores and thereafter next year slightly higher at INR 2,000 crores and then again 1,500.
Growth & demand: One, of course, I think if you really look at, you know, demand side, Quarter 1 FY27 was reasonably all right, despite having lot of issues externally and one of them was, you know, geopolitical situation which we are in.
Despite that, I think demand was better, industry has grown by about 8% or so.
And similarly on, you know, renewable energy front, AFR, on logistics front, and even on top- line, you know, elements like volume, premium products, geo mix and all.
Margins & costs: Capacity utilization last quarter industry level was on an average about 73%, 74%, couple of players higher than that and some of them were lower than that.
Yes, raw material cost is constant, it has not gone up with respect to last quarter, but fuel cost, packing cost, this is definitely I think is on increasing trend now.
So raw material consumption has gone up in SBS and that has impacted overall, you know, raw material cost inflation.
Capex & expansion: JK Lakshmi Cement Limited August 06, 2026 Overall installed capacity of cement in India after 11 million ton addition is about 725 million ton.
Durg it does include Durg because out of 5000 capex which the number we have given we are talking of about INR3000 crores for Durg and INR1500 crores for Northeast.
This capex number doesn't include the land acquisition cost which are presently doing for Nagor and Kutch.
Balance sheet & cash: One is on leverage part of it and second, cost impact which is going to be little more in Quarter 2 than what it was before.
We would not like to cross net debt to EBITDA 2.5x to at best 2.75x.
Risks & challenges: So, this is what just a brief, so there's a kind of, you know, uncertainty in terms of cost landscape and particularly on fuel part of it.
Now pet coke was kind of softening a bit little bit in between, but it has gone up shot up once again.
Now as I said before that on energy front, fuel front there is an uncertainty.

Guidance & outlook: Overall quarter 4 FY26 demand growth is estimated at about 6% to 6.5%, volume about 17% quarter -over-quarter driven by broad -based traction.

Now on outlook part of it, what we see volume growth during FY25-'26 was driven by, of course, housing demand, infrastructure and is likely to remain in the range of about 5.5% to 6% or 6.5%, this is what our estimation is.

We expect total capex in FY27 to be around INR1,500 crores to INR1,700 crores and close to INR2,000 crores in the next year when we would be also taking up the -- we have already started, but it will ramp up the land acquisition and the project in Kutch and Nagaur.
Growth & demand: During the financial year 2025 -'26, pan-India cement demand grew by about 7% to reach to about 480 million tons, estimated 480 million tons.
This is an improvement over 5% Y -o-Y demand growth recorded in 2024 -'25.
